data.description:
# Bound the memory sum on the rebar service host

The $0 half of epic `couped-subzero-wolf`. Nothing here resizes hardware; this is what makes
any instance size actually hold. Four enforcement points, each sized from measurement.

## Measured basis (CloudWatch `rebar/host`, i-00880b2c7f13527c5, 2026-09-03T17:00 -> 2026-09-05)

Per-container `container_memory_rss_bytes`, 48h Average / Maximum:

| service | avg | max |
|---|---|---|
| gerrit | 0.92 GB | 1.19 GB |
| mcp | 1.66 GB | **4.64 GB** |
| review-bot | 1.07 GB | **2.43 GB** |
| opcert | 0.041 GB | 0.048 GB |
| **sum of maxima** | | **8.31 GB** |

Physical RAM is 7.8 GiB = 8.37 GB. **The sum of observed per-container peaks is 99% of
physical memory**, with nothing left for the OS or page cache. `mem_available_percent`
hourly minima on the outage day: 11-13% sustained for seven hours.

The gate transients live INSIDE `mcp` and `review-bot` (both execute gates), which is why
their maxima are 4.3x and 15x their quiet baselines. `max_concurrent_gates` resolves to the
code default 4 and `rebar.toml` has no `[snapshot]` section; `docker-compose.yml` declares
no `mem_limit` on any of the four services; `gate_admission.py` admits on a count alone.

## The probe cannot be trusted to detect this (measured, and it changes deliverable 4)

Same probe run, hours 09-05 12:00-16:00 PDT: `mcp_healthy` (head of `observability.sh`)
published 7-12 samples/hour throughout, while `mem_available_percent` (tail) published
**zero datapoints for five consecutive hours**. Last 3h on a healthy idle box:
`mem_available_percent` 5/36 buckets (14%), `mcp_healthy` 29/36 (81%).

The probe never died — it is SIGTERM-ed on its 240s budget before reaching the memory read.
**The memory signal is anti-correlated with the condition it measures.** A `breaching`
alarm on a metric absent 73-86% of the time is a missing-data pager, not a memory detector.

Corollary this buys for free: head-metric present + memory absent = truncated;
head absent = probe dead. That discrimination needs no new signal.

## Changes

1. **`rebar.toml`**: add `[snapshot] max_concurrent_gates = 2`. Removes 2 x 739 MB
   (the measured per-gate peak, ADR 0112) from the permitted worst case: 8.31 -> 6.83 GB
   (82% of RAM), moving the available-memory floor from ~11% to ~18%. 2 rather than 1
   because deliverable 3 refuses the second slot when memory is already low, so the count
   need not carry the whole bound alone.

2. **`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`**: `mem_limit` on all four services.
   - `gerrit` **3072m** — reservation-driven, not usage-driven: `heapLimit 2g` +
     `packedGitLimit 1g` = 3 GiB configured (ADR 0112). Measured max 1.19 GB, so 2.6x
     headroom over observation; the limit honours the config ceiling.
   - `mcp` **2048m** — quiet baseline 0.97 GB + one gate slot 0.74 GB = 1.71 GB, 17%
     headroom. The 4.64 GB observed peak is 2.3x this limit, so that excursion now kills
     mcp loudly instead of letting the kernel choose gerrit.
   - `review-bot` **1280m** — quiet 0.16 GB + one gate 0.74 GB = 0.90 GB, 42% headroom.
   - `opcert` **256m** — 5x its observed 0.048 GB, flat across 48h.
   - Sum 6656 MiB = 6.5 GiB, leaving **1.3 GiB (17%)** of 7.8 GiB for OS and page cache.
   - Accepted tradeoff, stated rather than hidden: the shared counter caps gates at 2
     TOTAL but per-container limits cannot express a joint bound, so each container is
     sized for ONE concurrent gate. Both slots landing in one container exceeds that
     container's limit and OOM-kills it — a bounded, attributable failure, which is the
     point.

3. **`src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py`**: a `MemAvailable` floor read from `/proc/meminfo`,
   refusing with a retryable `LLMError` (never a verdict value) below **1024 MiB**. That is
   above the entire observed wedge band (13% of 7.8 GiB = 1.01 GB) and above one gate's
   739 MB peak plus margin. Reads `/proc/meminfo` directly, NOT CloudWatch and NOT psutil:
   it works on a laptop with no CI provider and adds no dependency. Absent `/proc/meminfo`
   (macOS) the check is inapplicable and stays silent; present-but-unreadable emits the
   existing disarm marker. The module docstring's claim that the counter "also bounds
   concurrent gate RSS" becomes true by construction.

4. **`infra/terraform/monitoring_membound.tf`**: two alarms, sized from measured coverage.
   - Threshold: `mem_available_percent < 15`, `treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"`,
     1 of 6 periods of 300s. 15% separates the 11-13% wedge band from every non-incident
     hourly minimum in the 48h window (lowest was 16%). `notBreaching` so absence never
     pages. Detection latency is degraded until the probe truncation fix lands; the
     re-tune target (3 of 6) is recorded in the file.
   - Dead-man: `mem_available_percent` with `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`,
     `datapoints_to_alarm == evaluation_periods = 36` at 300s = a 3-hour all-empty window.
     Sized from measurement, not a round number: across the 48h series the ONLY span of
     >= 3 hours with zero memory datapoints is the incident itself, and it would have
     fired ~3h into the 5-hour silence, before the wedge. Re-tune to 900-1800s once
     coverage recovers; recorded in the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 `[snapshot].max_concurrent_gates = 2` in `rebar.toml`, resolving to 2.
- [ ] AC2 All four compose services declare `mem_limit`; their sum is below 7 GiB.
- [ ] AC3 `gate_admission` refuses a gate when `MemAvailable` is below the floor, with
      retryable semantics, and admits when it is above. Refusal is never a verdict value.
- [ ] AC4 The memory check degrades to ADMIT when `/proc/meminfo` is absent.
- [ ] AC5 Both alarms exist and satisfy the `alarm-window-tuning.md` invariants
      (`test_alarm_window_tuning.py` passes unmodified).
- [ ] AC6 `terraform validate` passes. Terraform is NOT applied by this change.

## What this does NOT establish

- That memory exhaustion caused the 2026-09-05 wedge. It remains the leading candidate
  (`retiring-coronary-muntjac`); this change bounds it either way.
- Whether mcp's 4.64 GB peak is steady-state growth or allocator retention.
- The actual concurrent gate count in practice versus the permitted 4.
- Whether 15% is the right threshold beyond the 48h window measured; the margin to the
  lowest non-incident minimum is one percentage point.
data.title: Bound the memory sum on the rebar service host: gate concurrency, container limits, memory-aware admission, and honest alarms
